To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the α-domain of metallothionein shows luminescence properties similar to those of the intact metallothionin, but with a more compact and rigid Cu(I)-cluster structure.
the Cu-fragment of rat liver metalothionein-2 has a different luminescence behavior than the intact metallothionin, suggesting a more stable and compact luminophore in α-domain.
the Cu-thionein has a higher luminescence quantum yield compared to the α-domain, and the Cu-thioneins have more compact and stable clusters than the α-domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the luminescence properties of the Cu-fragments of rat liver metalloprotein.
the luminescence properties of Cu-thionein, a Cu(II) complex with metallothionein, and its chemically synthesized α-fragment.
the luminescence of metallothioneins and their fragments and their application for the determination of Cu(I) in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α-domain has a more rigid Cu-cluster than that in the intact metallothionin.
the α-domain is a more compact and more stable Cu-cluster than the intact metallothionin.
the α-domain is the main site for the luminescence of metallothionein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the luminescent Cu-thionein species is a cluster of Cu(I) ions coordinated to the cysteine residues of the polypeptide chain.
the luminescence of the α-domain is more stable than the intact metallothionin and the Cu(I) coordination of the α-domain can be considered as the first step of the Cu-thionein formation.
metallothioneins have the potential to be used as luminescent probes in biological systems and that the Cu-thionein is a suitable probe in the presence of high concentrations of Cu(I).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cu-thionein α-domain is a stable luminophore and can be used as an analytical tool for the determination of Cu(I) in biological samples.
metallothioneins can be used as a model system for the investigation of Cu(I) binding to peptides and proteins.
the luminescence properties of the Cu-fragment are different from those of the Cu-metallothionein and this difference is likely to reflect the different Cu-cluster structures of the two Cu-species.
